---
title: "Capstone report template"
---

Two pages maximum, plain Markdown, placed at `reports/<your-name>-<track>.md`. The
report is read by a facilitator and by one other participant. Write for them: assume
they did a different track.

## Required sections

### 1. Problem and model

State the model in equations (the generative process or SDE, the variational family or
the causal graph). Name the dataset and the ground truth available in it. Four to eight
lines.

### 2. What you built

List the functions implemented, in dependency order, with one sentence each. State which
checkpoint tests pass and which, if any, do not, with the failing assertion.

### 3. Experiment

One experiment beyond the checkpoint tests, chosen from the track-specific prompts below
or of your own design. Include: what you varied, what you measured, a table or a single
figure, and the result in one sentence. Fixed PRNG keys; report them.

### 4. What went wrong

The most expensive bug or misconception of the day, how you detected it, and what
diagnostic would have caught it sooner. This section is mandatory and is the part most
readers learn from.

### 5. Open question

One question your results raise that you could not answer in the time available, and a
sketch of the experiment that would answer it.

## Track-specific experiment prompts

**Track A — Flows.** (i) Depth versus fit: ELBO and KL to the HMC reference as a function
of the number of coupling layers (2, 4, 8). (ii) Funnel geometry: compare the fitted
flow's marginal over $\log\tau$ with HMC's and with mean-field VI's; quantify the tail
mass below $\log\tau = -2$. (iii) Importance-weighted ELBO with the flow as proposal: how
many samples until the effective sample size exceeds 50%?

**Track B — Diffusion.** (i) Sampler step count: Wasserstein or energy distance between
generated and held-out torsion angles as a function of the number of Euler–Maruyama
steps (50, 200, 1000). (ii) Likelihood: test log-likelihood from the probability-flow ODE
versus a Gaussian mixture fit with the same number of parameters. (iii) Noise schedule:
linear versus cosine $\beta(t)$, same budget.

**Track C — Causal.** (i) Identifiability: estimate the SCM coefficients from
observational data alone and show which counterfactual queries are sensitive to the
seasonality confounder being observed or not. (ii) Posterior over exogenous noise: for a
single week, show the abducted $U$ posterior and the counterfactual conversion
distribution under halved spend; compare with the closed-form answer. (iii) Misspecified
mechanisms: replace the linear traffic mechanism with a saturating one in the data, keep
the linear model, and quantify the counterfactual bias.

## Grading rubric (for facilitators)

| Criterion | Weight |
|---|---|
| Checkpoint tests pass | 30% |
| Experiment is well-posed and the result is stated correctly | 30% |
| "What went wrong" is specific and the proposed diagnostic is sound | 25% |
| Clarity: equations, tables and prose are precise and brief | 15% |
